newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Dec 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Dec 5.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories in its Thursday editions:
- The French government suspended its plan to sell Thomson S.A., the heavily indebted, state-owned electronics company.
- the Dow Jones industrial average lost 19.75 points, closing at 6,422.94.
- Ford Motor said its sales fell 2.2 percent in November.
- Retailers were generally upbeat on the eve of the holiday shopping season, the Federal Reserve reported.

- Joseph Hendricks, who operates one of the country's biggest chains of auto dealerships, was indicted in Ashville, N.C. on Federal charges of conspiring to bribe Honda officials to get extra cars and dealerships.
- Seven financial giants, including Chase Manhattan, have agreed to market the Mondex electronic cash product in the United States.
- National Westminster Bank said it would cut as many as 10,000 jobs, or 20 percent of its work force, in Britain over five years as it increases computer use in its branches.
- Soaring exports fueled German economic growth in the third quarter.
- Saga Petroleum of Norway agreed to acquire Santa Fe Exploration of Britain for $1.23 billion from Kuwait Petroleum.

- Northern Telecom shares have lost almost 5 percent of their value since Tuesday, the day Sprint Spectrum announced it would not meet its target for introducing its advanced wireless voice and data services.
